description: Creates the run row synchronously, then hands off to a background worker thread and returns immediately so the UI can begin polling without blocking the Streamlit script thread (ADR-006, ADR-017).
signature: def start_pipeline_async(db_path: Path, config: PipelineConfig, *, settings: Settings | None = None) -> str
docstring:
Start a new run in the background and return its id immediately.

Args:
    db_path: Never a connection (ADR-017). A short-lived connection is opened on the calling thread just to create the run row, then closed before the worker starts.
    config: This run's PipelineConfig. start_stage is normally ACQUISITION here; a non-ACQUISITION start_stage for a brand-new run_id is legal but unusual (a deliberate partial re-run is more commonly done via resume_run against an EXISTING run_id).
    settings: Loaded via config.load_settings() if not given.

Returns:
    The new run_id, available immediately (before the pipeline has done any real work).

Sequence:
    1. If settings is None, settings = config.load_settings().
    2. parameters_version = config.parameters_version(settings.parameters_path) -- a cheap file hash, computed before any parameter parsing/validation (see storage.create_run's own docstring for why this ordering matters).
    3. with storage.connect(db_path) as conn: run_id = storage.create_run(conn, config=config.to_dict(), parameters_version=parameters_version, trigger_type='manual', notes=config.notes) -- this connection is opened, used, and closed entirely on the calling thread, before the worker thread exists.
    4. cancel_event = threading.Event(); register (cancel_event, db_path) into _CANCEL_REGISTRY[run_id] under the module lock.
    5. Start a non-daemon threading.Thread whose target: opens its own connection via storage.connect(db_path) as its first statement, calls run_pipeline(conn, run_id, config, settings=settings, cancel_token=cancel_event) inside a try/except that catches every exception (an exception escaping a thread target is invisible -- the target itself already wrote the terminal status via run_pipeline before this outer catch, so the catch here only prevents a silent thread death, it does not re-handle status), and in a finally: removes run_id from _CANCEL_REGISTRY and closes its own connection.
    6. Return run_id, before the thread has necessarily done any work.
preconditions: db_path's parent directory exists or is creatable (delegated to storage.get_connection)
run_id is not already registered in _CANCEL_REGISTRY (impossible by construction since create_run always returns a fresh id)
postconditions: The returned run_id has a runs row with status 'pending' or 'running' immediately after this call returns, readable by a separate connection on any thread
is_running(run_id) is True immediately after this call returns and remains True until the worker's finally block runs
No sqlite3.Connection object is returned or held by this function past step 3

edge_cases.expected_behavior: not detected here -- start_pipeline_async only computes the cheap parameters_version hash, never calls load_parameters; the failure surfaces later inside the worker as PreflightError, with the run row already visible in the run list as required
propagates directly to the caller (the UI's Start button handler); no thread is started, no run_id is returned, since there is nothing to poll for

edge_cases.input: The worker thread's target raises an exception that escapes run_pipeline's own status-writing try/except (a bug in run_pipeline itself)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: the outer catch in the thread target logs it (e.g. to stderr) so it is not silently swallowed, but does not attempt to write a status a second time; this is a defense against a genuinely unexpected failure mode, not the normal path

edge_cases.input: Called twice in rapid succession from the same Streamlit session (double-click on Start)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: each call creates its own independent run_id and its own worker; the UI's own 'Start disabled while active_run_ids() is non-empty' rule (07_ui.module_spec.json) is what prevents this in practice, not this function

unit_tests.name: test_returns_run_id_immediately
unit_tests.description: start_pipeline_async returns before the stubbed pipeline has finished (asserted with a stage stub that blocks on an Event the test controls).
unit_tests.expected: call returns quickly; run_id is a valid, freshly created id

unit_tests.name: test_run_row_visible_before_return
unit_tests.description: Immediately after return, a separate connection can read the run row via storage.get_run.
unit_tests.expected: get_run(run_id) returns a RunRecord with status in {'pending','running'}

unit_tests.name: test_is_running_true_then_false_after_completion
unit_tests.description: is_running(run_id) is True right after start, and becomes False once the stubbed pipeline completes.
unit_tests.expected: True immediately, False after the worker's finally runs

unit_tests.name: test_no_connection_returned_or_leaked
unit_tests.description: A connection-factory spy asserts exactly one open/close pair on the calling thread for run creation, separate from the worker thread's own open/close pair.
unit_tests.expected: two independent open/close pairs, none crossing threads

unit_tests.name: test_create_run_failure_starts_no_thread
unit_tests.description: If storage.create_run raises, no thread is started and the exception propagates.
